claims.statement: Polish insurance-industry guidance identifies water damage from plumbing or heating failures among the most common causes of home losses and treats home assistance, including a plumber, as an established optional insurance feature. This supports a real loss event and response need, but does not quantify Polish frequency, severity, or preventable share.

Under Poland's Act on Ownership of Premises, a community board manages and represents the community, but actions beyond ordinary management require an owners' resolution and authorization; entry to a private unit is mandated only for specified maintenance, repair, common-property emergency, or additional-installation purposes. The statute does not itself grant an outside property manager blanket authority to sell exclusive telemetry and repair-dispatch rights over private-unit plumbing.

No evidence establishes that a specific Polish housing community or cooperative will approve the required resolution, secure representative private-unit installation and ongoing access, and grant this entrant an exclusive building-wide telemetry and dispatch agreement.

PKO Ubezpieczenia currently describes a home-insurance bundle in which connected devices can trigger an immediate phone notification, insurer follow-up, and organized specialist help including a plumber; its home-assistance limit is PLN 5,000 per policy period. This is a direct incumbent substitute for alert-plus-dispatch, even if its sensing architecture is not identical to the candidate's proposed building telemetry.

TUW ran a 2025 offer giving a Wi-Fi leak sensor and home assistance with a home policy whose minimum annual premium was PLN 400. The promotion has ended, but it demonstrates that a Polish carrier can bundle a basic sensor at zero explicit customer price and anchors willingness to pay below a separately visible monthly prevention fee.

E2 Insurance currently markets an insurer-ready white-label workflow spanning leak detection, customer notification, assistance escalation, incident closure, portfolio reporting, retention controls, and integrations. The proposed alert-to-dispatch workflow is therefore available from a regional European supplier and is not itself a unique control mechanism.

Ondo's July 2026 regulatory announcement reports 167,000 active LeakBots, 26 carrier partners, more than 60% reduction in mains-water claim frequency in matched carrier data, and an expected positive insurer ROI at USD 60 per home per year. This is strong company-reported evidence that some insurers will repeatedly pay for an integrated detection-and-repair service, but it is not Polish contract evidence and the underlying white paper is co-authored by the vendor.

The closest scaled public comparator reported FY2026 revenue of GBP 4.645 million, gross contribution of GBP 0.219 million, a 4.7% gross operating margin, and a GBP 7.259 million pre-tax loss while serving 144,507 active devices at year-end; it also completed a multi-part refinancing in July 2026. These figures directly challenge the candidate's untested 30-45% blended gross-margin expectation during rollout and a bootstrap path based on PLN 100,000, although they do not prove Polish conservative economics impossible.

Ondo reports approximately USD 197 lifetime value and USD 148 net profit after acquisition cost per active US device over an average 6.5-year device life, based on 1.27% monthly churn. This supports positive mature repeat economics in one market, but the implied net profit is spread over many years and is not evidence for PLN 10 net monthly revenue per Polish apartment.
No sourced Polish carrier commitment validates PLN 8-20 per apartment per month, hardware prepayment, a measured-loss bonus, renewal linkage, or a 12-month pilot-to-contract conversion path.

The Polish Financial Ombudsman explains that insurers should reimburse rational, documented mitigation costs after an insured peril occurs, including plumber interventions and urgent repairs. This supports a reimbursable emergency-dispatch event, but it does not establish an insurer budget for continuous pre-loss monitoring subscriptions.

Poland's data-protection regulator states, in the analogous smart-meter context, that time-granular utility consumption reveals when and how a person uses a service and therefore requires a clear controller, access scope, purpose, retention period, security, and safeguards around automated processing. Apartment water-flow telemetry cannot be treated as an unencumbered proprietary dataset.

Article 35 of Poland's insurance and reinsurance act makes insurers, employees, and entities through which insurance activities are performed responsible for secrecy concerning individual insurance contracts. A contractor can participate under the carrier's controlled arrangement, but ownership, reuse, and portability of claim outcomes for an entrant's moat cannot be presumed.

There is no contract or term sheet granting the entrant durable rights to join unit-level telemetry, repair records, and insurer claim outcomes; reuse those data across carriers; retain derived features after termination; or port the trained model away from a white-label vendor.

A 2025 peer-reviewed smart-home insurance paper did not observe which homes had water-leak detectors: it estimated 7% detector adoption and then estimated water-claim reductions from a prior source. Its favorable water table is therefore modeled rather than direct device-linked claims evidence, illustrating why non-Polish headline savings should not be imported as pilot proof.

No Polish baseline or power calculation establishes how many building-years are needed to separate true claim-frequency and severity reduction from selection bias, regression to the mean, building age, plumbing condition, resident response, and weather effects.

If the entrant uses third-party white-label sensing and platform infrastructure, the supplier owns or controls much of the detection stack while the insurer controls policy and claim outcomes. Without negotiated IP, data, model-training, audit, continuity, and exit rights, the entrant's own mechanism is primarily local contracting and repair orchestration rather than a proprietary anomaly-detection loop.

Ondo defines active revenue-generating devices to exclude units whose policy was cancelled or which lost signal or battery connectivity. Connectivity, batteries, policy churn, and field replacement are therefore recurring service-economics variables, not one-time installation details.

The EU Cyber Resilience Act covers network-connected products and creates cybersecurity design, vulnerability-handling, market-surveillance, and economic-operator obligations, with full application from December 2027 and some reporting duties earlier. Any white-label hardware and software contract must allocate ongoing compliance, update, incident-reporting, and support responsibility across the device life.

No supplier quote or draft agreement validates certified device availability, per-unit landed cost, installation labor, connectivity fees, battery and failure replacement, warranty, product liability, firmware support, telemetry access, API limits, or model portability for Polish multifamily buildings.

No signed Polish plumbing-network SLA or quote establishes 24/7 geographic coverage, time-to-attend, night and holiday pricing, false-positive callout cost, capacity during bursts, repair authorization, resident no-access handling, or liability allocation.

There is no evidence for Polish insurer procurement duration, acquisition cost per property manager or carrier, pilot sales conversion, hardware working-capital timing, or payback under conservative activation and renewal rates.

Ondo reported only 0.9% penetration of 15.4 million addressable households under contract at FY2026 year-end despite 144,507 active devices. A carrier contract therefore does not imply rapid unit activation, and the candidate's 50,000-unit path needs an explicit enrollment, access, installation, and activation funnel.

contrary_evidence: [s07-ondo-fy26] The closest scaled comparator reported only 4.7% gross operating margin and a GBP 7.259 million pre-tax loss in FY2026, not the proposed 30-45% blended rollout margin.
[s05-pko-smart-home] PKO already bundles connected-device alerts, insurer follow-up, and organized plumber assistance in a Polish home-insurance product.
[s06-tuw-sensor-promo] A Polish carrier has given a Wi-Fi leak detector to qualifying policyholders at zero explicit device price, creating a difficult price anchor for a separate monthly fee.

[s08-e2-white-label] A regional European supplier already offers a white-label insurer platform covering detection, assistance escalation, incident records, and portfolio reporting, so workflow ownership is not unique.

[s02-locale-ownership-act] Polish community governance and private-unit access are conditional; a property-manager signature alone is not proven to convey exclusive building-wide telemetry and dispatch control.

[s03-uodo-smart-meter; s04-insurance-secrecy-act] Utility telemetry and insurance outcomes carry privacy and secrecy constraints, so the proposed cross-domain data moat exists only if explicit contracts confer usable rights.

[s09-peer-reviewed-method] Even peer-reviewed favorable water-loss estimates can be modeled from assumed detector adoption rather than observed device-linked claims, weakening transfer of headline savings to Poland.
[s07-ondo-fy26] The category leader had activated only 0.9% of households under contract, showing that signed distribution and actual protected-unit scale are materially different milestones.
